messages:
Rina: quick heads up - new bootcamp users hitting a weird parse error when using jsonMode + function-calls in the JS sample app. seems to be related to an extra newline chunk in streaming output. repro and logs below.

Rina: repro (node):
```js
const c = new RedwoodSDK({ jsonMode: true, streaming: true });
await c.chat.complete({ model: 'rw-mini', messages: [{role:'user', content:'invoke tool'}], functions: [{ name: 'echo', parameters: { type: 'object', properties: { t: { type: 'string' } }, required:['t'] } }] });
```

Rina: observed stream chunks:
```
chunk1: '{"name":"echo","arguments":{"t":"hi"}}'
chunk2: '\n'
assembled: '{"name":"echo","arguments":{"t":"hi"}}\n'
JSON.parse error: Unexpected token \n in JSON at position 34
```

Omar: newline as separate chunk? hmm. which sdk version and samplekit build?

Rina: js-sdk@0.8.3, samplekit v0.16-local (npm start). py-sdk not hitting this.

Devina: possible causes: streaming serializer emits newline as delimiter for human-readability then the joiner doesn't trim it before parse. py-sdk's parser strips whitespace. JS parser fails because we pass assembled string straight into JSON.parse.

Omar: fix idea: trim whitespace on assembled string before parse, but better to avoid emitting standalone newline chunk. add serializer test to assert no chunk is solely whitespace.

Rina: added a tiny hack in my local: assembled = assembled.trim(); works around it. pushed as test-only change to fork.

Devina: agree we should patch serializer. also add a unit that simulates streaming fragmentation where a token boundary splits on \n so we keep parity coverage.

Rina: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samplekit/pull/212 - two-line fix in sdk/streaming/joiner.ts + test.

build-bot: ci: samplekit-e2e build #210 queued

Omar: once PR is green, let's cut a patch to samplekit and add a short note in onboarding docs: "If you see JSON parse errors in quickstart, try --no-stream or update samplekit". We should avoid surfacing trim hack in docs as permanent fix.

Devina: also add a small parity test comparing JS and Py assembled outputs for streaming function calls to catch regressions.

Rina: thanks team. I'll follow up with the PR PR comments after CI. :sparkles:
